chunks: And you are but one of two types of men:

Either you are a man whose soul is generous in giving out rights, so why do you hide from fulfilling an obligatory right that you give, or a noble deed that you render? Or you are afflicted with stinginess, in which case how quickly do people cease asking you when they lose hope of your generosity! Despite the fact that most of the people's needs from you are matters that do not involve hardship for you, such as complaining of an injustice, or seeking fairness in a transaction.
ai.seo_question: What are the two types of leaders described in Nahj al-Balagha regarding their interaction with the people's needs?
ai.summary: In this passage from his famous letter to Malik al-Ashtar, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses a rhetorical dichotomy to critique the governor's perceived aloofness, contrasting the expected accessibility of a generous leader with the swift disengagement of subjects from a stingy one. This reflects the Shia political ideal of the ruler as a servant of the people, where 'hijab' (seclusion) is only justified if it stems from a lack of capacity to give, rather than a lack of will. The emphasis on minor needs like redressing grievances highlights the practical application of justice (adl) in daily governance.
